functions.name: readstat_error_message
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for a ReadStat error code. Useful for logging or surfacing parse/write errors.
requirements: error_code must be a valid readstat_error_t value.

functions.name: readstat_get_row_count
functions.description: Gets the number of rows/observations from metadata. Returns -1 if unknown (e.g., XPORT, POR, or some SAV files).
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_var_count
functions.description: Gets the number of variables/columns from metadata.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_creation_time
functions.description: Returns the file creation time from metadata.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_modified_time
functions.description: Returns the last modified time from metadata.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_file_format_version
functions.description: Returns the detected file format version from metadata.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_file_format_is_64bit
functions.description: Indicates whether the parsed file format is 64-bit (applies to formats where relevant).
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_compression
functions.description: Returns the compression mode of the source file (none/rows/binary).
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_endianness
functions.description: Returns the endianness of the source file.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_get_table_name
functions.description: Returns the table/dataset name from metadata (when available).
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_get_file_label
functions.description: Returns the file label/description from metadata (when available).
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_get_file_encoding
functions.description: Returns the detected or configured file character encoding.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_get_multiple_response_sets
functions.description: Returns an array of multiple-response set descriptors discovered in the file (SPSS feature).
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.
Use readstat_get_multiple_response_sets_length() to determine the array length.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_get_multiple_response_sets_length
functions.description: Returns the number of multiple-response sets in the metadata.
requirements: metadata must be a valid, initialized readstat_metadata_t pointer produced by the parser.

functions.name: readstat_value_type
functions.description: Returns the concrete storage type of a value (string/int8/int16/int32/float/double/string_ref).
requirements: value must be obtained from a ReadStat value callback or variable missing range accessor.

functions.name: readstat_value_type_class
functions.description: Returns the type class (string or numeric) of a value.
requirements: value must be obtained from a ReadStat value callback or variable missing range accessor.

functions.name: readstat_value_is_missing
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the value should be treated as missing. Considers system missing, tagged missing, and SPSS defined-missing ranges.
requirements: value must be from a ReadStat callback or accessor.
variable must be the corresponding variable for the value when checking defined-missing rules; may be NULL if only system/tagged missing is relevant (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_value_is_system_missing
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the value is system-missing (typically NaN delivered to handlers).
requirements: value must be from a ReadStat callback or accessor.

functions.name: readstat_value_is_tagged_missing
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the value is a tagged-missing value (Stata/SAS).
requirements: value must be from a ReadStat callback or accessor.

functions.name: readstat_value_is_defined_missing
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the value is missing due to variable-defined missing ranges (SPSS).
requirements: value must be from a ReadStat callback or accessor.
variable must be a valid pointer to the variable whose missingness rules apply.

functions.name: readstat_value_tag
functions.description: Returns the tag character for a tagged-missing value (e.g., 'a', 'b'). Undefined for non-tagged values.
requirements: value should be checked with readstat_value_is_tagged_missing() before using the tag (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_int8_value
functions.description: Extracts the int8 value from a readstat_value_t.
requirements: value.type must be READSTAT_TYPE_INT8 (or numeric convertible) for meaningful results (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_int16_value
functions.description: Extracts the int16 value from a readstat_value_t.
requirements: value.type should be a numeric type for meaningful results (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_int32_value
functions.description: Extracts the int32 value from a readstat_value_t.
requirements: value.type should be a numeric type for meaningful results (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_float_value
functions.description: Extracts the float value from a readstat_value_t.
requirements: value.type should be float or convertible numeric for meaningful results (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_double_value
functions.description: Extracts the double value from a readstat_value_t.
requirements: value.type should be double or convertible numeric for meaningful results (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_string_value
functions.description: Extracts a const char* from a string value. For string refs, upstream code may resolve to actual strings during parsing/writing.
requirements: value.type must be READSTAT_TYPE_STRING for meaningful results (inferred).
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_type_class
functions.description: Maps a concrete readstat_type_t to its class (string or numeric).
requirements: type must be a valid readstat_type_t.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_index
functions.description: Returns the variable’s index in file order.
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_index_after_skipping
functions.description: Returns the index accounting for skipped variables (when variable handler returns READSTAT_HANDLER_SKIP_VARIABLE).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_name
functions.description: Returns the variable name.
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_label
functions.description: Returns the variable label (if present).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_format
functions.description: Returns the display/storage format string (format depends on file type).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_type
functions.description: Returns the storage type for the variable.
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_type_class
functions.description: Returns the type class (string or numeric) for the variable.
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_storage_width
functions.description: Returns the storage width in bytes (relevant for strings; also doubles in SAS XPORT).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_display_width
functions.description: Returns the suggested display width for the variable (if available).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_measure
functions.description: Returns the variable’s measurement level (nominal/ordinal/scale/unknown).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_alignment
functions.description: Returns the variable’s alignment (left/center/right/unknown).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_missing_ranges_count
functions.description: Returns the count of defined-missing ranges for this variable (SPSS).
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_missing_range_lo
functions.description: Returns the low endpoint/value of the i-th defined-missing range for the variable.
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.
i must be within [0, count) where count is readstat_variable_get_missing_ranges_count(variable).

functions.name: readstat_variable_get_missing_range_hi
functions.description: Returns the high endpoint/value of the i-th defined-missing range for the variable.
requirements: variable must be a non-NULL pointer obtained from callbacks or writer APIs.
i must be within [0, count) where count is readstat_variable_get_missing_ranges_count(variable).

functions.name: readstat_parser_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a parser instance with default settings and no handlers.
requirements: Caller must later free with readstat_parser_free().

functions.name: readstat_parser_free
functions.description: Frees a parser and its resources.
requirements: parser must be a parser returned by readstat_parser_init() or NULL.
Parser must not be used after this call.

functions.name: readstat_io_free
functions.description: Frees a readstat_io_t object and (optionally) its io_ctx if flagged.
requirements: io must be either NULL or a pointer created/owned by the parser/IO setup.
Do not use io after freeing.

functions.name: readstat_set_metadata_handler
functions.description: Registers the metadata callback invoked at the start of parsing with file metadata.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser.
metadata_handler may be NULL to unset.
Set before readstat_parse_*().

functions.name: readstat_set_note_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback for file notes/documents where applicable.
requirements: parser must be valid.
note_handler may be NULL to unset.
Set before readstat_parse_*().

functions.name: readstat_set_variable_handler
functions.description: Registers the variable declaration callback; returning READSTAT_HANDLER_SKIP_VARIABLE skips value callbacks for that variable.
requirements: parser must be valid.
variable_handler may be NULL to unset.
Set before readstat_parse_*().

functions.name: readstat_set_fweight_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback for frequency weight variables (if present).
requirements: parser must be valid.
fweight_handler may be NULL to unset.
Set before readstat_parse_*().

functions.name: readstat_set_value_handler
functions.description: Registers the per-cell value callback invoked for each observation-variable pair (subject to skipping).
requirements: parser must be valid.
value_handler may be NULL to unset.
Set before readstat_parse_*().

functions.name: readstat_set_value_label_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback for value labels encountered in the file.
requirements: parser must be valid.
value_label_handler may be NULL to unset.
Set before or during parse initialization, before labels are processed.

functions.name: readstat_set_error_handler
functions.description: Registers an error handler to receive textual error messages during parsing.
requirements: parser must be valid.
error_handler may be NULL to unset.
Do not throw from C callbacks into C unless your embedding supports it (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_set_progress_handler
functions.description: Registers a progress callback called with [0.0,1.0] progress estimates.
requirements: parser must be valid.
progress_handler may be NULL to unset.

functions.name: readstat_set_open_handler
functions.description: Sets a custom IO open handler to override default file IO.
requirements: parser must be valid.
open_handler may be NULL to unset.
If custom IO is used, you should set a consistent set of open/close/seek/read/update/io_ctx before parsing (inferred).

functions.name: readstat_set_close_handler
functions.description: Sets a custom IO close handler.
requirements: parser must be valid.
close_handler may be NULL to unset.

functions.name: readstat_set_seek_handler
functions.description: Sets a custom IO seek handler.
requirements: parser must be valid.
seek_handler may be NULL to unset.

functions.name: readstat_set_read_handler
functions.description: Sets a custom IO read handler.
requirements: parser must be valid.
read_handler may be NULL to unset.

functions.name: readstat_set_update_handler
functions.description: Sets a custom IO update handler for progress integration with custom IO.
requirements: parser must be valid.
update_handler may be NULL to unset.

functions.name: readstat_set_io_ctx
functions.description: Sets an IO context pointer passed to IO handlers.
requirements: parser must be valid.
If set, the lifetime and thread-safety of io_ctx are managed by the caller unless the library flags it for free (see readstat_io_free).

functions.name: readstat_set_file_character_encoding
functions.description: Overrides the file character encoding detection (e.g., for pre-14 Stata using system encodings).
requirements: parser must be valid.
encoding must be an iconv-compatible name (as per comment).
Call before parse begins.

functions.name: readstat_set_handler_character_encoding
functions.description: Sets the output encoding for handler strings; defaults to UTF-8. Pass NULL to disable transliteration.
requirements: parser must be valid.
Call before parse begins.

functions.name: readstat_set_row_limit
functions.description: Limits the number of rows to parse (for sampling or early termination).
requirements: parser must be valid.
row_limit must be non-negative (inferred).
Set before parse begins.

functions.name: readstat_set_row_offset
functions.description: Skips a number of initial rows before invoking value callbacks.
requirements: parser must be valid.
row_offset must be non-negative (inferred).
Set before parse begins.

functions.name: readstat_parse_dta
functions.description: Parses a Stata .dta file at path using the configured parser and invokes callbacks.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured as needed (handlers/IO/encodings).
path must point to a readable .dta file.
user_ctx is passed through to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_parse_sav
functions.description: Parses an SPSS .sav (or .zsav) file.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured.
path must point to a readable SAV/ZSAV file.
user_ctx is passed through to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_parse_por
functions.description: Parses an SPSS portable .por file.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured.
path must point to a readable POR file.
user_ctx is passed through to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_parse_sas7bdat
functions.description: Parses a SAS .sas7bdat data file.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured.
path must point to a readable sas7bdat file.
user_ctx is passed through to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_parse_sas7bcat
functions.description: Parses a SAS .sas7bcat catalog file (value labels and formats).
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured.
path must point to a readable sas7bcat file.
user_ctx is passed through to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_parse_xport
functions.description: Parses a SAS Transport (XPORT) file.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured.
path must point to a readable XPORT file.
user_ctx is passed through to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_parse_sas_commands
functions.description: Parses SAS command/script file into a schema describing how to read a corresponding text data file.
requirements: parser must be initialized and configured as needed for reading command file.
filepath must reference a readable command file.
outError may be non-NULL to receive an error code; must point to writable memory if provided.
Returned schema must be freed with readstat_schema_free().

functions.name: readstat_parse_spss_commands
functions.description: Parses SPSS command/script file into a schema for parsing a text data file.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
filepath must reference a readable command file.
outError may be non-NULL to receive an error code; must point to writable memory if provided.
Returned schema must be freed with readstat_schema_free().

functions.name: readstat_parse_stata_dictionary
functions.description: Parses a Stata dictionary into a schema for parsing a text data file.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
filepath must reference a readable dictionary file.
outError may be non-NULL to receive an error code; must point to writable memory if provided.
Returned schema must be freed with readstat_schema_free().

functions.name: readstat_parse_txt
functions.signature: readstat_error_t readstat_parse_txt(readstat_parser_t *parser, const char *filename, readstat_schema_t *schema, void *user_ctx);
functions.description: Parses a delimited/plain-text data file according to a previously generated schema (from commands/dictionary).
requirements: parser must be initialized and have appropriate handlers set.
schema must be a valid schema from readstat_parse_*_commands or readstat_parse_stata_dictionary.
filename must reference a readable text data file.
user_ctx is passed to callbacks.

functions.name: readstat_schema_free
functions.description: Frees a schema returned by the parse_*_commands/dictionary functions.
requirements: schema may be NULL; otherwise must be a schema previously returned by this API.
Do not use schema after freeing.

functions.name: readstat_writer_init
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a writer for creating files in supported formats.
requirements: Caller must later free with readstat_writer_free() or readstat_end_writing() then free.

functions.name: readstat_set_data_writer
functions.description: Sets the output byte sink callback for the writer. The data_writer must behave like write(2), returning bytes written or -1 on error.
requirements: writer must be a valid writer.
data_writer must be non-NULL and safe for repeated calls during writing.

functions.name: readstat_add_label_set
functions.description: Creates a named value label set for later association with variables.
requirements: writer must be initialized.
type must be a valid readstat_type_t matching values to be labeled.
name must be a non-NULL, non-empty C string (inferred).
Returned set is owned by the writer; do not free directly.

functions.name: readstat_label_double_value
functions.description: Adds or updates a label for a specific double value in the label set.
requirements: label_set must be created by readstat_add_label_set() with a numeric type.

import io
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for minimally valid Stata .dta files (versions 117-119)
# Target: readstat_parse_dta expects a readable filename from FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We return bytes representing a small, coherent .dta file to trigger deeper parsing paths.
# Strategy:
# - Prefer Stata 117 layout (widely supported) with 1-3 variables and few rows.
# - Build consistent headers, map, variable descriptors, value labels (optional), and data.
# - Keep within 4096 bytes.
# Note: This is not an exhaustive writer but aims to produce structurally valid files.

# References distilled from Stata DTA 117/118/119 public docs:
# - magic b"<stata_dta>\n\r\n\032"
# - header with release, byteorder, filetype, unused, nvar, nobs, data_label, time_stamp
# - map: 15 64-bit offsets (we can fill reasonably)
# - variable_types, varnames, sortlist, formats, value_label_names, variable_labels
# - characteristics (empty okay)
# - data section
# - strls (optional)
# - value labels section (optional)

# Utility encoders

def u8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>B', x)

def i16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>h', x)

def u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>H', x)

def u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>I', x)

def i32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>i', x)

def u64(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>Q', x)

def enc_cstr(s: str, n: int) -> bytes:
    # NUL-terminated, max n bytes including NUL
    bs = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    bs = bs[: max(0, n-1)]
    return bs + b"\x00" * (n - len(bs))

def enc_name(s: str, n: int) -> bytes:
    # For varnames and labels where fixed size without forced NUL at end (Stata uses NUL-terminated inside fixed field)
    bs = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    if len(bs) >= n:
        bs = bs[: n-1]
    bs = bs + b"\x00"
    return bs + b"\x00" * (n - len(bs)) if len(bs) < n else bs

# Stata 117 type codes: 65530=STRL, 32768+len=STR#, 251=double, 255=LONGSTR? but for 117 we will use numeric and small str
# Simpler: use types: 251 (double), 252 (float), 253 (long), 254 (int), 255 (byte), and strings encoded as 32768+len

NUM_TYPES = {
    'double': 251,
    'float': 252,
    'long': 253,
    'int': 254,
    'byte': 255,
}

# For string: code = 32768 + length (1..2045)

def str_type_code(length: int) -> int:
    return 32768 + max(1, min(2045, length))

# Format strings are ASCII up to 49+1 bytes, NUL-terminated.

class Dta117Builder:
    def __init__(self, seed: int):
        self.r = random.Random(seed)

    def rand_var_name(self, i: int) -> str:
        # Stata names: start with letter or _; letters, digits, _; up to 32
        base = ['x','y','z','v','w','u','t']
        name = (self.r.choice(base) + str(i))[:31]
        return name

    def make(self) -> bytes:
        r = self.r
        nvar = r.randint(1, 3)
        nobs = r.randint(1, 5)
        # Choose mix of types
        var_kinds = []
        for i in range(nvar):
            kind = r.choice(['double','float','long','int','byte','str'])
            if kind == 'str':
                slen = r.choice([5,8,12,20])
                var_kinds.append(('str', slen))
            else:
                var_kinds.append((kind, None))
        # Build sections as bytearray then compute map
        sections = {}
        out = bytearray()

        # Header
        magic = b"<stata_dta>\n\r\n\x1a"
        header = bytearray()
        header += magic
        header += b"\n"  # newline after magic block per spec
        # Release 117
        header += b"<header>\n"
        header += b"\t" + b"release\n"
        header += i32(117)
        header += b"\t" + b"byteorder\n"
        header += i32(1)  # 1 = big endian per spec for network? Stata uses 1 for MSF? ReadStat handles both; use 1
        header += b"\t" + b"filetype\n"
        header += i32(1)
        header += b"\t" + b"unused\n"
        header += i32(0)
        header += b"\t" + b"nvar\n"
        header += i32(nvar)
        header += b"\t" + b"nobs\n"
        header += i32(nobs)
        header += b"\t" + b"data_label\n"
        dl = "Fuzz DTA"
        header += u8(len(dl)) + dl.encode('utf-8')
        header += b"\t" + b"time_stamp\n"
        ts = "01 Jan 2000 00:00"
        header += u8(len(ts)) + ts.encode('ascii')
        header += b"</header>\n"

        # Placeholder map; will fill after sections built
        map_bytes = bytearray()
        map_bytes += b"<map>\n"
        # 15 offsets (start of each major block) as 64-bit
        offsets = [0]*15
        for _ in range(15):
            map_bytes += u64(0)
        map_bytes += b"</map>\n"

        # Variable types
        vt = bytearray(b"<variable_types>\n")
        for kind, slen in var_kinds:
            if kind == 'str':
                code = str_type_code(slen)
            else:
                code = NUM_TYPES[kind]
            vt += u16(code)
        vt += b"</variable_types>\n"

        # Var names
        vn = bytearray(b"<varnames>\n")
        for i in range(nvar):
            name = self.rand_var_name(i)
            vn += enc_name(name, 33)
        vn += b"</varnames>\n"

        # Sortlist (nvar+1 shorts). Zero-terminated list; we keep zeros.
        sl = bytearray(b"<sortlist>\n")
        for _ in range(nvar+1):
            sl += i16(0)
        sl += b"</sortlist>\n"

        # Formats (49+1 each)
        fm = bytearray(b"<formats>\n")
        for kind, slen in var_kinds:
            if kind == 'str':
                fmt = f"%{slen}s"
            elif kind == 'double':
                fmt = "%9.0g"
            elif kind == 'float':
                fmt = "%9.0g"
            elif kind == 'long':
                fmt = "%9.0g"
            elif kind == 'int':
                fmt = "%9.0g"
            else:
                fmt = "%9.0g"
            bs = fmt.encode('ascii')
            if len(bs) > 49:
                bs = bs[:49]
            fm += bs + b"\x00" * (50 - len(bs))
        fm += b"</formats>\n"

        # Value label names (33 bytes each, NUL-terminated). We leave empty with single NUL.
        vln = bytearray(b"<value_label_names>\n")
        for _ in range(nvar):
            vln += b"\x00" * 33
        vln += b"</value_label_names>\n"

        # Variable labels (81 bytes each)
        vl = bytearray(b"<variable_labels>\n")
        for i in range(nvar):
            lbl = f"Var {i}"
            bs = lbl.encode('utf-8')[:80]
            vl += bs + b"\x00" * (81 - len(bs))
        vl += b"</variable_labels>\n"

        # Characteristics: empty block
        ch = bytearray(b"<characteristics>\n</characteristics>\n")

        # Data
        data = bytearray(b"<data>\n")
        # For each observation, write values in var order according to type sizes
        for _row in range(nobs):
            for kind, slen in var_kinds:
                if kind == 'str':
                    # write fixed-length string with padding
                    s = ''.join(r.choice('abcXYZ012') for _ in range(slen))
                    bs = s.encode('ascii')
                    if len(bs) < slen:
                        bs += b" " * (slen - len(bs))
                    data += bs
                elif kind == 'double':
                    data += struct.pack('>d', r.uniform(-1000, 1000))
                elif kind == 'float':
                    data += struct.pack('>f', r.uniform(-1000, 1000))
                elif kind == 'long':
                    data += i32(r.randint(-100000, 100000))
                elif kind == 'int':
                    data += i16(r.randint(-30000, 30000))
                elif kind == 'byte':
                    data += struct.pack('>b', r.randint(-100, 100))
                else:
                    data += struct.pack('>d', 0.0)
        data += b"</data>\n"

        # Strls: none
        strls = bytearray(b"<strls>\n</strls>\n")

        # Value labels section: empty
        vls = bytearray(b"<value_labels>\n</value_labels>\n")

        # Assemble with map offsets
        pieces = [
            (b"header", bytes(header)),
            (b"map", bytes(map_bytes)),
            (b"variable_types", bytes(vt)),
            (b"varnames", bytes(vn)),
            (b"sortlist", bytes(sl)),
            (b"formats", bytes(fm)),

import random
import struct
import time

# This generator produces a minimal but valid SPSS SAV file (classic uncompressed)
# sufficient for ReadStat to parse. It supports small variability while remaining valid.
# We construct:
# - File header (Record Type 2 header)
# - Machine integer info (Record Type 3, subtype 3)
# - Machine floating-point info (Record Type 3, subtype 4)
# - Variable records (Record Type 7) for N variables (1..4)
# - Value label records (optional, but we omit to keep minimal)
# - Documents (omitted)
# - Info records: VARIABLE DISPLAY PARAMETERS (optional, omitted)
# - End-of-file dictionary termination (Record Type 999)
# - Case data (Record Type 8) for R rows (1..5)
# This layout follows SPSS SAV file structure sufficient for basic parsers. Values are simple.
# We avoid compression and exotic features. Strings are ASCII and names fit 8 chars.

# Constants per SAV format
SPSS_SYSFILE_HEADER_REC_TYPE = 2
SPSS_DICT_TERMINATOR = 999
SPSS_VAR_RECORD_TYPE = 7
SPSS_DATA_RECORD_TYPE = 8
SPSS_INFO_RECORD_TYPE = 3

# Variable type: 0 = numeric, >0 = string width
# We will use either numeric or short strings (<=8) for simplicity


def _pad8(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # pad to multiple of 8 bytes with spaces
    pad = (-len(s)) & 7
    return s + (b" " * pad)


def _spss_name(base: str) -> bytes:
    # SPSS variable names up to 8 in older versions; we keep <=8 and uppercase letters/digits/underscore
    b = base.upper().encode('ascii')[:8]
    b = b + b"_" * (max(1, len(b)) - len(b)) if len(b) == 0 else b
    b = b + b" " * (8 - len(b))
    return b


def _write_header(nvars: int, ncases: int) -> bytes:
    # Record type (int32), prod name (60 bytes), layout code(int32), nvars(int32), compression(int32), weight index(int32), ncases(int32), bias(double)
    rec_type = struct.pack('<i', SPSS_SYSFILE_HEADER_REC_TYPE)
    prod_name = b"@(#) IBM SPSS STATISTICS                        "
    prod_name = prod_name[:60].ljust(60, b" ")
    layout_code = 2  # classic
    compression = 0  # uncompressed
    weight_index = 0
    bias = 100.0  # compression bias (used when compressed, still present)
    # Creation date/time (9 + 8 bytes ASCII), file label (64), padding(3)
    tm = time.gmtime()
    date_str = time.strftime('%d %b %y', tm).upper().encode('ascii')
    date_str = date_str[:9].ljust(9, b' ')
    time_str = time.strftime('%H:%M:%S', tm).encode('ascii')
    time_str = time_str[:8].ljust(8, b' ')
    file_label = b"FUZZ SAV".ljust(64, b' ')
    padding3 = b"\x00\x00\x00"
    header = (
        rec_type +
        prod_name +
        struct.pack('<i', layout_code) +
        struct.pack('<i', nvars) +
        struct.pack('<i', compression) +
        struct.pack('<i', weight_index) +
        struct.pack('<i', ncases) +
        struct.pack('<d', bias) +
        date_str + time_str + file_label + padding3
    )
    return header


def _write_machine_integer_info() -> bytes:
    # Record type 3, subtype 3, size=4, count=8, payload of 8 int32s per spec
    # Little endian, version info etc. We provide plausible values.
    rec_type = struct.pack('<h', SPSS_INFO_RECORD_TYPE)
    subtype = struct.pack('<h', 3)
    size = struct.pack('<h', 4)
    count = struct.pack('<h', 8)
    # fields: machine integer info
    # 1: sysmis (int), 2: highest missing (int), 3: lowest missing (int) — historic; we set zeros
    # 4: file layout code (2), 5: case size (computed later, but not strictly required by modern readers),
    # 6: compression code (0), 7: weight index (0), 8: ncases (can be -1 unknown or actual)
    vals = [0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    payload = b"".join(struct.pack('<i', v) for v in vals)
    return rec_type + subtype + size + count + payload


def _write_machine_floating_info() -> bytes:
    # Record type 3, subtype 4, size=8, count=3: sysmis (double), highest, lowest
    rec_type = struct.pack('<h', SPSS_INFO_RECORD_TYPE)
    subtype = struct.pack('<h', 4)
    size = struct.pack('<h', 8)
    count = struct.pack('<h', 3)
    payload = struct.pack('<ddd', float('nan'), 1.0e38, -1.0e38)
    return rec_type + subtype + size + count + payload


def _write_variable_records(var_defs):
    # For each variable, write Record Type 7 blocks
    out = b""
    for v in var_defs:
        var_type, name8, label = v['type'], v['name8'], v['label']
        # Basic variable record (type, has_label, n_missing, print, write, name[8])
        has_label = 1 if label else 0
        n_missing = 0
        print_fmt = 0  # default auto
        write_fmt = 0
        out += struct.pack('<i', SPSS_VAR_RECORD_TYPE)
        out += struct.pack('<i', var_type)
        out += struct.pack('<i', has_label)
        out += struct.pack('<i', n_missing)
        out += struct.pack('<i', print_fmt)
        out += struct.pack('<i', write_fmt)
        out += name8
        if has_label:
            lb = label.encode('utf-8')[:255]
            lb_len = len(lb)
            out += struct.pack('<i', lb_len)
            out += _pad8(lb)
        # No missing values definitions appended
    return out


def _write_dictionary_terminator() -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<i', SPSS_DICT_TERMINATOR)


def _write_cases(var_defs, ncases, rng) -> bytes:
    out = b""
    # Data record indicator
    out += struct.pack('<i', SPSS_DATA_RECORD_TYPE)
    # Then case data: for each case, for each variable: numeric (8-byte double), string blocks of 8-char chunks
    for _ in range(ncases):
        for v in var_defs:
            if v['type'] == 0:
                # numeric
                val = rng.uniform(-10.0, 10.0)
                out += struct.pack('<d', val)
            else:
                width = v['type']
                s = v['gen']()
                bs = s.encode('utf-8')[:width]
                bs = bs.ljust(width, b' ')
                # strings stored in 8-byte segments
                for i in range(0, width, 8):
                    out += bs[i:i+8]
    return out


def _make_var_defs(rng, nvars):
    var_defs = []
    for i in range(nvars):
        is_string = rng.random() < 0.5
        if is_string:
            width = rng.choice([4, 8, 12, 16])
            # names like STR1, STR2
            name = f"STR{i+1}"
            def gen(width=width, rng=rng):
                alphabet = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789'
                k = rng.randint(1, min(6, width))
                return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(k))
            var_defs.append({
                'type': width,
                'name8': _spss_name(name),
                'label': f"String var {i+1}",
                'gen': gen
            })
        else:
            name = f"NUM{i+1}"
            def gen_num(rng=rng):
                return rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0)
            var_defs.append({
                'type': 0,
                'name8': _spss_name(name),
                'label': f"Numeric var {i+1}",
                'gen': gen_num
            })
    return var_defs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    nvars = rng.randint(1, 4)
    ncases = rng.randint(1, 5)
    var_defs = _make_var_defs(rng, nvars)

    buf = b""
    buf += _write_header(nvars, ncases)
    buf += _write_machine_integer_info()
    buf += _write_machine_floating_info()
    buf += _write_variable_records(var_defs)
    buf += _write_dictionary_terminator()
    buf += _write_cases(var_defs, ncases, rng)

    # Ensure size constraint
    return buf[:4096]

import random

from typing import List

# Generator for SPSS Portable (.por) files
# We aim to create minimal yet valid-ish POR files that ReadStat can parse.
# We construct a small dataset with 1-3 variables and a few cases, using
# documented POR token structure from SPSS (simplified, focusing on common subset).
# Note: ReadStat accepts upper/lowercase tokens; we stick to canonical forms.

# POR format quick primer (simplified):
# - Header line: starts with ASCII "SPSS PORT FILE" and version/date/time blocks
# - Then records (cards) each beginning with a letter indicating type and data that follows
#   Common records include: "A" (version/date/time), "I" (integer delimiter),
#   "S" (variable info), "V" (variable names), "F" (variable formats),
#   "N" (number of cases), "D" (data), "E" (end).
# Here we synthesize a compact, typical sequence that many parsers accept.
# We encode numbers in the portable textual numeric form used by POR (base-30-like encoding is internal
# to classic SPSS POR). However, ReadStat implements the actual parsing and accepts canonical decimal
# textual encodings found in widely seen PORs for simple values. We will use simple decimal tokens for data lines.
# Our construction mirrors simple PORs produced by SPSS with short ASCII fields.

# Safety: keep total size under 4096 bytes.

ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # SPSS variable names: start with letter, then letters/digits/underscore; up to 64 in modern SPSS,
    # but POR often limits to 8. We'll use 1-8.
    first = rng.choice(ALPHABET)
    rest_chars = ALPHABET + "_0123456789"
    rest = "".join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(max(0, length-1)))
    return first + rest

def _date_token(ts: int) -> str:
    # POR header date/time tokens often in YYYYMMDD HH:MM:SS
    t = time.gmtime(ts)
    return f"{t.tm_year:04d}{t.tm_mon:02d}{t.tm_mday:02d} {t.tm_hour:02d}:{t.tm_min:02d}:{t.tm_sec:02d}"

def _make_header(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # First line marker with a newline; many PORs start with: "SPSS PORT FILE" followed by version/date/time lines
    # We'll emit classic banner and an A-record with version/date/time.
    ver = rng.choice(["4.0", "4.1", "5.0"])  # benign versions
    created = _date_token(int(time.time()) - rng.randint(0, 10_000_000))
    modified = _date_token(int(time.time()))
    # Header banner is exactly 20 bytes in classic files, but readers accept a line starting with "SPSS PORT FILE".
    banner = "SPSS PORT FILE\n"
    a_record = f"A{ver} {created} {modified}\n"
    return banner + a_record

def _format_from_type(t: str, width: int, decimals: int) -> str:
    # Simple formats: F for numeric, A for string
    if t == 'N':
        return f"F{width}.{decimals}"
    else:
        return f"A{width}"

def _make_variables(rng: random.Random, var_count: int):
    # Build variables metadata lines: S (var count), then V (names), F (formats)
    names: List[str] = []
    types: List[str] = []  # 'N' or 'A'
    widths: List[int] = []
    decimals: List[int] = []
    for i in range(var_count):
        name_len = rng.randint(3, 8)
        name = _rand_name(rng, name_len)
        # ensure unique names
        while name in names:
            name = _rand_name(rng, name_len)
        names.append(name)
        is_string = rng.random() < 0.4  # some strings
        if is_string:
            types.append('A')
            widths.append(rng.randint(4, 16))
            decimals.append(0)
        else:
            types.append('N')
            widths.append(rng.choice([8, 10, 12]))
            decimals.append(rng.choice([0, 2]))
    # S record: variable count
    s_record = f"S{var_count}\n"
    # V record: names and types separated by spaces
    v_parts = []
    for n, t in zip(names, types):
        v_parts.append(n)
        v_parts.append(t)
    v_record = "V" + " ".join(v_parts) + "\n"
    # F record: formats per variable
    f_parts = []
    for t, w, d in zip(types, widths, decimals):
        f_parts.append(_format_from_type(t, w, d))
    f_record = "F" + " ".join(f_parts) + "\n"
    return s_record + v_record + f_record, names, types, widths, decimals

def _rand_numeric(rng: random.Random, decimals: int) -> str:
    # Generate varied numeric values within readable ranges
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.2:
        val = 0
    elif choice < 0.4:
        val = rng.randint(-100, 100)
    elif choice < 0.7:
        val = rng.uniform(-1e3, 1e3)
    else:
        val = rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
    if decimals > 0:
        return f"{val:.{decimals}f}"
    else:
        return f"{int(round(val))}"

def _rand_string(rng: random.Random, width: int) -> str:
    # Create ASCII strings respecting width (POR pads or trims; we'll keep <= width)
    length = rng.randint(0, max(0, width))
    chars = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./"
    s = "".join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    return s

def _make_cases(rng: random.Random, types: List[str], widths: List[int], decimals: List[int], ncases: int) -> str:
    # N record: number of cases
    n_record = f"N{ncases}\n"
    # D records: one per case, values separated by tabs or spaces
    lines = []
    for _ in range(ncases):
        vals = []
        for t, w, d in zip(types, widths, decimals):
            if t == 'N':
                vals.append(_rand_numeric(rng, d))
            else:
                sval = _rand_string(rng, w)
                # In POR, strings that include spaces should be quoted; we will quote all strings to be safe
                q = sval.replace('"', "'")
                vals.append(f'"{q}"')
        lines.append("D" + " ".join(vals) + "\n")
    # E record: end
    e_record = "E\n"
    return n_record + "".join(lines) + e_record

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose small dataset dimensions
    var_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    ncases = rng.randint(1, 5)

    parts = []
    parts.append(_make_header(rng))
    vars_section, names, types, widths, decimals = _make_variables(rng, var_count)
    parts.append(vars_section)
    parts.append(_make_cases(rng, types, widths, decimals, ncases))

    data = ("".join(parts)).encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure size bound
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

# Goal: Generate minimally valid-looking SAS sas7bdat bytes with high variability while staying coherent.
# We vary many header fields, page sizes/counts (kept to 1 due to 4096 cap), timestamps, names, encodings,
# and sprinkle random padding bytes in reserved areas. All values are internally consistent so parsers
# are more likely to accept. Output limited to <= 4096 bytes.

MAGIC = b"SAS7BDAT"  # 8 bytes
ALIGN_32 = 4
ALIGN_64 = 8
PAGE_TYPE_DATA = 0x0101


def _pack(endian_le: bool, fmt: str, *vals: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(("<" if endian_le else ">") + fmt, *vals)


def _rand_ascii(rnd: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_"
    return bytes(rnd.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _mk_header(rnd: random.Random, little_endian: bool, align: int, page_len: int, page_count: int,
               created: float, modified: float, ds_name: bytes, encoding: bytes,
               platform_blob: bytes, extra_pad: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Build a 1024-byte header with coherent key fields and randomized metadata in safe ranges
    buf = bytearray(1024)
    # Magic
    buf[0:8] = MAGIC
    # Alignment and endianness flags (heuristic placeholders)
    buf[8] = 0x33 if align == ALIGN_64 else 0x00
    buf[9] = 0x01 if little_endian else 0x00

    # Platform blob (put right after 0x0A for some readers)
    pb = platform_blob[:0x0A]
    buf[0x0A:0x0A+len(pb)] = pb

    # Header length (0x3C) and page length (0x40)
    struct.pack_into(("<" if little_endian else ">") + 'I', buf, 0x3C, 1024)
    struct.pack_into(("<" if little_endian else ">") + 'I', buf, 0x40, page_len)
    # Page count (0x48)
    struct.pack_into(("<" if little_endian else ">") + 'I', buf, 0x48, page_count)

    # Created/Modified as doubles at 0x20 and 0x28
    struct.pack_into(("<" if little_endian else ">") + 'd', buf, 0x20, float(created))
    struct.pack_into(("<" if little_endian else ">") + 'd', buf, 0x28, float(modified))

    # Encoding at 0x54..
    e = encoding[:24]
    buf[0x54:0x54+len(e)] = e

    # Dataset name around 0x150
    dsn = ds_name[:24]
    buf[0x150:0x150+len(dsn)] = dsn

    # Sprinkle some pad randomness in reserved zones to diversify outputs without breaking structure
    # Zone A
    za_off = 0x60
    za_len = min(32, len(extra_pad))
    buf[za_off:za_off+za_len] = extra_pad[:za_len]
    # Zone B
    zb_off = 0x180
    zb_len = min(48, len(extra_pad) - za_len)
    if zb_len > 0:
        buf[zb_off:zb_off+zb_len] = extra_pad[za_len:za_len+zb_len]

    return bytes(buf)


def _mk_page_header(little_endian: bool, page_type: int, page_len: int, seq: int, block_count: int = 1) -> bytes:
    ph = bytearray(32)
    endian = "<" if little_endian else ">"
    struct.pack_into(endian + 'H', ph, 0x00, page_type)
    struct.pack_into(endian + 'H', ph, 0x02, block_count)
    struct.pack_into(endian + 'H', ph, 0x04, 0)  # subheaders count
    struct.pack_into(endian + 'H', ph, 0x06, 0)
    struct.pack_into(endian + 'I', ph, 0x08, page_len)
    struct.pack_into(endian + 'I', ph, 0x0C, seq)
    # remaining reserved zero
    return bytes(ph)


def _mk_data_page(rnd: random.Random, little_endian: bool, page_len: int, seq: int, row_marker: bytes) -> bytes:
    ph = _mk_page_header(little_endian, PAGE_TYPE_DATA, page_len, seq)
    payload_len = page_len - len(ph)
    payload = bytearray(payload_len)
    # Put a small marker and some random-looking but ASCII-safe bytes
    marker = row_marker[:24]
    payload[0:len(marker)] = marker
    # Add a few 4-byte integers to exercise numeric reading
    for i in range(6):
        off = 64 + i * 4
        if off + 4 <= payload_len:
            struct.pack_into("<I" if little_endian else ">I", payload, off, rnd.randrange(0, 1 << 31))
    # Fill a small area with random ascii to mimic row bytes
    start = 128
    plen = min(64, payload_len - start)
    if plen > 0:
        payload[start:start+plen] = _rand_ascii(rnd, plen)
    return ph + bytes(payload)


def _choose_encoding(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    encs = [b"UTF-8", b"windows-1252", b"latin1", b"UTF-16LE", b"mac-roman"]
    return rnd.choice(encs)


def _choose_platform_blob(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Short platform signature-like blobs to add diversity. Not authoritative, but harmless.
    opts = [
        b"WIN\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
        b"LINUX\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
        b"AIX\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
        b"HPUX\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
        b"SUNOS\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
    ]
    # Slight randomization
    base = bytearray(rnd.choice(opts))
    if len(base) < 10:
        base.extend(b"\x00" * (10 - len(base)))
    # Flip a byte or two in harmless range
    for _ in range(rnd.randrange(0, 3)):
        idx = rnd.randrange(0, min(10, len(base)))
        base[idx] ^= rnd.randrange(0, 4)
    return bytes(base[:10])


def _build_sas7bdat(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Endianness and alignment variation
    little = rnd.choice([True, False])
    align = rnd.choice([ALIGN_64, ALIGN_32])

    # Choose page length; ensure final file <= 4096, so stick with 2048 or 3072 or 4096
    page_len = rnd.choice([2048, 3072, 4096])
    page_count = 1

    # Timestamps in SAS seconds since 1960-01-01; choose plausible range
    day = 24 * 60 * 60
    created = float(rnd.randrange(0, 365 * 80) * day + rnd.randrange(0, day))
    modified = created + rnd.randrange(0, 48 * 3600)

    # Names and encoding
    ds_name = _rand_ascii(rnd, rnd.randrange(4, 16))
    encoding = _choose_encoding(rnd)
    platform_blob = _choose_platform_blob(rnd)

    # Random padding bytes to diversify header reserved areas
    extra_pad = bytes(rnd.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(96))

    header = _mk_header(rnd, little, align, page_len, page_count, created, modified, ds_name, encoding, platform_blob, extra_pad)

    # Page sequence starts at 1 (common)
    row_marker = b"ROWDATA_" + _rand_ascii(rnd, 8)
    page = _mk_data_page(rnd, little, page_len, 1, row_marker)

    data = header + page
    # Ensure cap
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_sas7bdat(rnd)

def _fixstr(s: str, length: int) -> bytes:

    return b.ljust(length, b' ')

# Helper to write an 8-byte SAS datetime (seconds from 01JAN1960:00:00:00)
# We'll just set to a reasonable positive number

def _sas_dt(seconds: int) -> bytes:
    # SAS stores as IEEE 754 double (big endian or little). We'll choose little endian here.
    return struct.pack('<d', float(seconds))

# Build a simple label entry block: a fake record representing a format with labels
# This is NOT the precise spec, but aims to be well-formed enough for a tolerant parser.

def _build_label_block(fmt_name: str, fmt_type: int, labels: List[tuple]) -> bytes:
    # Block layout (custom, consistent within this generator):
    # [u32 block_type=1][u32 block_len][fmt_name(32)][u32 fmt_type][u32 nlabels]
    # For each label: [val_len u16][val bytes][lab_len u16][label bytes]
    block = io.BytesIO()
    block.write(struct.pack('<I', 1))
    payload = io.BytesIO()
    payload.write(_fixstr(fmt_name, 32))
    payload.write(struct.pack('<I', fmt_type))
    payload.write(struct.pack('<I', len(labels)))
    for val, lab in labels:
        v = str(val).encode('utf-8')
        l = lab.encode('utf-8')
        payload.write(struct.pack('<H', len(v)))
        payload.write(v)
        payload.write(struct.pack('<H', len(l)))
        payload.write(l)
    p = payload.getvalue()
    block.write(struct.pack('<I', len(p)))
    block.write(p)
    return block.getvalue()

# Build a simple format properties block

def _build_format_props_block(fmt_name: str, width: int, decimals: int, category: str) -> bytes:
    # [u32 block_type=2][u32 block_len][name(32)][u32 width][u32 decimals][category(16)]
    payload = io.BytesIO()
    payload.write(_fixstr(fmt_name, 32))
    payload.write(struct.pack('<I', width))
    payload.write(struct.pack('<I', decimals))
    payload.write(_fixstr(category, 16))
    p = payload.getvalue()
    return struct.pack('<II', 2, len(p)) + p

# File header builder: create a plausible SAS7BCAT header

def _build_header(endianness: str, osname: str, encoding: str, created_sec: int, modified_sec: int, page_size: int, page_count: int) -> bytes:
    # We'll mimic the SAS7BDAT style header fields adapted for cat, enough for ReadStat to sniff
    # Layout (simplified):
    # magic(8) + file_type(8) + endianness(1) + oserr(1) + pad(6)
    # osname(16) + encoding(16) + created(8) + modified(8)
    # page_size(u32) + page_count(u32) + hdrlen(u16) + pad to 1024
    bio = io.BytesIO()
    bio.write(MAGIC)
    bio.write(_fixstr('SAS FILE ', 8))
    bio.write(b'L' if endianness == 'le' else b'B')
    bio.write(b'\x00')
    bio.write(b'\x00' * 6)
    bio.write(_fixstr(osname, 16))
    bio.write(_fixstr(encoding, 16))
    bio.write(_sas_dt(created_sec))
    bio.write(_sas_dt(modified_sec))
    bio.write(struct.pack('<I', page_size))
    bio.write(struct.pack('<I', page_count))
    bio.write(struct.pack('<H', 256))
    # Pad header to first page boundary (page_size)
    cur = bio.tell()
    if cur < page_size:
        bio.write(b'\x00' * (page_size - cur))
    return bio.getvalue()

# Build pages: concatenate blocks into pages with simple page headers

def _build_pages(blocks: List[bytes], page_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Each page: [u32 page_type=0xFFFEE001][u32 block_count][blocks packed]
    # We split blocks across pages if needed.
    out = io.BytesIO()
    cur = io.BytesIO()
    page_blocks = []

    def flush_page():
        nonlocal cur, page_blocks
        payload = cur.getvalue()
        hdr = struct.pack('<II', 0xFFFEE001, len(page_blocks))
        page = hdr + payload
        # pad to page size
        if len(page) < page_size:
            page += b'\x00' * (page_size - len(page))
        out.write(page)
        cur = io.BytesIO()
        page_blocks = []

    for b in blocks:
        # If current page would overflow, flush
        header_len = 8 if not page_blocks else 0  # first time we add page header on flush, but for sizing, just ensure payload
        if cur.tell() + len(b) + header_len > page_size - 8:  # leave room for header on flush
            flush_page()
        cur.write(b)
        page_blocks.append(1)
    if page_blocks:
        flush_page()
    return out.getvalue()

# Main generator

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose endianness and page size
    endianness = 'le' if rnd.choice([True, False]) else 'be'
    page_size = rnd.choice([1024, 2048, 4096])

    # Header metadata
    osname = rnd.choice(['LINUX', 'WIN', 'AIX', 'HPUX', 'SUN'])
    encoding = rnd.choice(['UTF-8', 'WINDOWS-1252', 'LATIN1'])
    created = 60 * 60 * 24 * rnd.randint(20000, 30000)  # some days after SAS epoch
    modified = created + rnd.randint(0, 60 * 60 * 24 * 30)

    # Build a few formats
    fmt_blocks = []

    # Numeric format with integer labels
    num_fmt_name = rnd.choice(['FMTNUM', 'AGEFMT', 'SCORE'])
    num_labels = []
    for i in range(rnd.randint(3, 8)):
        val = rnd.randint(-5, 20)
        lab = rnd.choice(['Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Missing', 'Yes', 'No']) + ('' if rnd.random() < 0.5 else f"_{i}")
        num_labels.append((val, lab))
    fmt_blocks.append(_build_label_block(num_fmt_name, 1, num_labels))
    fmt_blocks.append(_build_format_props_block(num_fmt_name, width=rnd.randint(4, 12), decimals=rnd.randint(0, 3), category='NUMERIC'))

    # String format with string labels
    str_fmt_name = rnd.choice(['FMTSTR', 'STATE', 'GENDER'])
    str_labels_src = [
        ('M', 'Male'), ('F', 'Female'), ('U', 'Unknown'),
        ('Y', 'Yes'), ('N', 'No'), ('NA', 'Missing')
    ]
    rnd.shuffle(str_labels_src)
    str_labels = str_labels_src[:rnd.randint(3, 6)]
    fmt_blocks.append(_build_label_block(str_fmt_name, 2, str_labels))
    fmt_blocks.append(_build_format_props_block(str_fmt_name, width=rnd.randint(2, 8), decimals=0, category='CHAR'))

    # Possibly add a date/time related format
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        dt_fmt_name = rnd.choice(['DATEFMT', 'DTFMT'])
        dt_labels = [
            ('2020-01-01', 'Start'),
            ('2020-12-31', 'End'),
            ('', 'Missing')
        ]
        fmt_blocks.append(_build_label_block(dt_fmt_name, 2, dt_labels))
        fmt_blocks.append(_build_format_props_block(dt_fmt_name, width=10, decimals=0, category='DATE'))

    # Assemble pages
    pages = _build_pages(fmt_blocks, page_size)

    # Compute page count (number of page_size chunks after header)
    header = _build_header(endianness, osname, encoding, created, modified, page_size, max(1, len(pages) // page_size))

    return (header + pages)[:4096]

import random
import struct
import time
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for minimal-yet-valid SAS XPORT (V5) file with one dataset and a few variables/rows.
# The fuzzer stub passes our bytes as a filename referencing a temp file containing this buffer.
# We aim to produce valid XPORT V5 according to SAS technical doc, with 80-byte card images.
# Records used: HEADER (LIBRARY), MEMBER (SASDATA), NAMES, LABELS, OBS with numeric/string.
# Note: Keep strictly 80-byte records and uppercase ASCII in headers.

CARD = 80

def pad80(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    return s.ljust(CARD, b' ')

def format_date(ts: int) -> bytes:
    # SAS XPORT wants date like DDMMMYY:HH:MM:SS in uppercase
    t = time.gmtime(ts)
    mmm = [b'JAN',b'FEB',b'MAR',b'APR',b'MAY',b'JUN',b'JUL',b'AUG',b'SEP',b'OCT',b'NOV',b'DEC'][t.tm_mon-1]
    return (f"{t.tm_mday:02d}".encode('ascii') + mmm + f"{(t.tm_year % 100):02d}".encode('ascii') +
            b":" + f"{t.tm_hour:02d}".encode('ascii') + b":" + f"{t.tm_min:02d}".encode('ascii') + b":" + f"{t.tm_sec:02d}".encode('ascii'))

def card_keyword(kw: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Keywords must be at start and uppercase. Fill rest with spaces.
    return pad80(kw)

def to_ebcdic_ascii(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # XPORT uses ASCII uppercase in headers; dataset and var names uppercased and space-padded.
    return s.upper()

def name_field(name: str, width: int) -> bytes:
    return to_ebcdic_ascii(name.encode('ascii')[:width]).ljust(width, b' ')

def num_to_ibm_double(val: float) -> bytes:
    # SAS XPORT V5 stores numeric as 8-byte IBM 370 FP (big-endian). Implement minimal conversion.
    # Convert IEEE 754 double to IBM 370: base16 exponent, 7-byte fraction.
    # This simplistic converter handles normals and zero; NaN/inf mapped to zero.
    import math
    if not math.isfinite(val):
        return b"\x00"*8
    if val == 0.0:
        return b"\x00"*8
    sign = 0x00
    if val < 0:
        sign = 0x80
        val = -val
    # Normalize to [0.5,1) in base 16 by shifting exponent
    exp2 = math.frexp(val)  # val = m * 2**e, m in [0.5,1)
    m, e2 = exp2
    # Convert base-2 exponent to base-16 (each step of 4 bits)
    # val = m * 2**e2 = (m * 16**k) * 2**(e2-4k)
    # Choose k so that 0.0625 <= m*2**(e2-4k) < 1 in base16 normal form (fraction in [0,1))
    k = (e2 + 3) // 4  # ceil(e2/4)
    e16 = e2 - 4*k
    frac = m * (2**e16)
    # Now val = frac * 16**k, want 0.0625<=frac<1; adjust if needed
    while frac >= 1.0:
        frac /= 16.0
        k += 1
    while frac < 0.0625:
        frac *= 16.0
        k -= 1
    # IBM exponent is offset 64
    ibm_exp = k + 64
    if ibm_exp <= 0:
        return b"\x00"*8
    if ibm_exp >= 127:
        # overflow to max
        ibm_exp = 126
    # Fraction is 56 bits (7 bytes) of fraction after the implied leading 0.x
    frac_int = int(frac * (1 << 56)) & ((1<<56)-1)
    b0 = (sign | (ibm_exp & 0x7F)).to_bytes(1,'big')
    bfrac = frac_int.to_bytes(7, 'big')
    return b0 + bfrac

def make_header(libname: str, memname: str, dslabel: str, created: int, modified: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += card_keyword(b'HEADER RECORD*******LIBRARY HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!000000000000000000000000000000  ')
    out += pad80(b'SAS     SAS     SASLIB  ' + name_field(libname,8) + format_date(created).ljust(24,b' ') + format_date(modified).ljust(24,b' '))
    out += pad80(b'                                                ')
    out += card_keyword(b'HEADER RECORD*******MEMBER  HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!000000000000000001600000000140  ')
    out += pad80(b'SAS     SAS     SASDATA ' + name_field(memname,8) + format_date(created).ljust(24,b' ') + format_date(modified).ljust(24,b' '))
    out += pad80(b'                                                ')
    out += card_keyword(b'HEADER RECORD*******DSCRPTR HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!000000000000000000000000000000  ')
    out += pad80(b'SAS     SAS     SASDATA ' + name_field(memname,8) + name_field(dslabel,40))
    out += pad80(b'                                                ')
    return bytes(out)

def make_names(vars: List[Tuple[str,str,int,int]]) -> bytes:
    # vars: list of (name, label, type, length). type: 'NUM' or 'CHAR', using 'NUM' for numeric.
    out = bytearray()
    out += card_keyword(b'HEADER RECORD*******NAMESTR HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!000000000000000000000000000000  ')
    count = len(vars)
    # Each NAMESTR is 140 bytes
    # NAMESTR layout (simplified V5):
    # 0: type (1=NUM, 2=CHAR) 2 bytes
    # 2: length (for char), 2 bytes
    # 4: name 8 bytes
    # 12: label 40 bytes
    # remaining pad to 140
    for name, label, typ, length in vars:
        tcode = 1 if typ == 'NUM' else 2
        rec = bytearray(140)
        rec[0:2] = struct.pack('>H', tcode)
        rec[2:4] = struct.pack('>H', max(0, length if typ=='CHAR' else 0))
        rec[4:12] = name_field(name,8)
        rec[12:52] = name_field(label,40)
        out += rec
    # Trailer card after NAMESTR block
    out += card_keyword(b'HEADER RECORD*******OBS     HEADER RECORD!!!!!!!000000000000000000000000000000  ')
    return bytes(out)

def make_obs(vars: List[Tuple[str,str,int,int]], rows: List[List[object]]) -> bytes:
    # Each observation is contiguous values: numeric as 8-byte IBM double, char as fixed width.
    out = bytearray()
    for r in rows:
        for (name,label,typ,length), val in zip(vars, r):
            if typ == 'NUM':
                out += num_to_ibm_double(float(val))
            else:
                s = str(val).encode('ascii', 'ignore')[:length]
                out += s.ljust(length, b' ')
        # Pad each observation to 80-byte boundary if needed
        pad = (-len(out)) % CARD
        if pad:
            out += b' ' * pad
    return bytes(out)

def build_xport(libname: str, memname: str, dslabel: str, vars: List[Tuple[str,str,int,int]], rows: List[List[object]], created: int, modified: int) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    parts.append(make_header(libname, memname, dslabel, created, modified))
    parts.append(make_names(vars))
    parts.append(make_obs(vars, rows))
    return b''.join(parts)

NUM = 'NUM'
CHAR = 'CHAR'

def random_ident(rng: random.Random, minlen: int, maxlen: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    chars = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_'
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length)).upper()
    # Ensure starts with letter
    if not s[0].isalpha():
        s = 'A' + s[1:]
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Random metadata
    libname = random_ident(rng, 3, 8)
    memname = random_ident(rng, 3, 8)
    dslabel = ("DATASET " + random_ident(rng, 3, 8))[:40]
    now = int(time.time())
    created = now - rng.randint(0, 10_000_000)
    modified = created + rng.randint(0, 100_000)

    # Build variables: mix of numeric and char with safe widths
    var_list: List[Tuple[str,str,int,int]] = []
    var_count = rng.randint(2, 5)
    for i in range(var_count):
        name = random_ident(rng, 3, 8)
        label = ("VAR " + name)[:40]
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            var_list.append((name, label, NUM, 8))  # numeric occupies 8 bytes
        else:
            width = rng.choice([4,8,12,16,24,32])
            var_list.append((name, label, CHAR, width))

    # Rows of data
    row_count = rng.randint(1, 10)
    rows: List[List[object]] = []
    for _ in range(row_count):
        r = []
        for (name,label,typ,length) in var_list:
            if typ == NUM:
                # choose varied numeric values
                choice = rng.random()
                if choice < 0.2:
                    v = 0.0
                elif choice < 0.4:
                    v = rng.randint(-1000, 1000)
                elif choice < 0.7:
                    v = rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
                else:
                    v = rng.uniform(0, 1) * (16 ** rng.randint(-10, 10))
                r.append(v)
            else:
                # ASCII strings within width
                base = random_ident(rng, 1, min(8, max(1, length)))
                if length > len(base) and rng.random() < 0.5:
                    base += '_' + random_ident(rng, 1, min(8, max(1, length - len(base) - 1)))
                r.append(base[:length])
        rows.append(r)

    data = build_xport(libname, memname, dslabel, var_list, rows, created, modified)
    # Ensure size cap
    return data[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for Stata dictionary (.dct) files describing fixed-width text
# Our goal: produce valid, interesting dictionaries that exercise various
# field types, formats, variable widths, row/col layouts, and options.
# We keep bytes <= 4096.

# Stata dictionary syntax (modern flavor):
#   dictionary using "data.txt" {
#     _column(1) byte    v1   "%8.0g"
#     _column(2) int     v2   "%9.0g"
#     _column(4) long    v3   "%12.0g"
#     _column(9) float   v4   "%9.0g"
#     _column(18) double v5   "%10.0g"
#     _column(30) str10  s1   "%10s"
#     _column(41) strL   sL
#     _column(42) %9s    s2   // legacy style width-as-format
#   }
# Lines may include labels via label("..."). Quoted names/labels may include spaces.
# Comments `/* ... */` and `// ...` may appear.

# We generate a header with encoding/byteorder occasionally, then a set of variable
# lines covering numeric, short/long strings, very long strL, and with/without formats.

NUMERIC_TYPES = [
    ("byte", 1), ("int", 2), ("long", 4), ("float", 4), ("double", 8)
]

STRING_WIDTH_CHOICES = [1,2,3,4,5,8,10,12,20,32,80,244]

QUOTES = ['"', "'"]

FMT_NUMERIC = ["%8.0g", "%9.0g", "%10.0g", "%12.0g", "%8.2f", "%9.1f", "%10.3f"]
FMT_STRING = ["%s", "%8s", "%10s", "%20s"]

ENCODINGS = ["utf-8", "latin1", "mac"]
BYTEORDERS = ["MSF1", "LSF1"]  # Most/Least-significant-first markers used by Stata

RESERVED_NAMES = ["_cons", "if", "in", "using", "byte", "int", "long", "float", "double"]


def rand_ident(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    # produce a Stata-friendly variable name (starts with letter/_; letters, digits, _)
    # Keep length within 32 chars
    prefix = r.choice(['v', 'x', 'y', 'z', '_'])
    mid = base[: max(1, 8)]
    tail = ''.join(r.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_') for _ in range(r.randint(0, 6)))
    name = (prefix + mid + tail)[:32]
    if name in RESERVED_NAMES:
        name = prefix + "_" + name
    return name


def qstr(r: random.Random, text: str) -> str:
    q = r.choice(QUOTES)
    inner = text.replace(q, q + q) if q == '"' else text.replace(q, q + q)
    return f"{q}{inner}{q}"


def gen_header(r: random.Random, data_name: str) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    # Optional version header
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        enc = r.choice(ENCODINGS)
        bo = r.choice(BYTEORDERS)
        lines.append(f"#delim ;") if r.random() < 0.15 else None
        lines.append(f"/* encoding and byteorder hints */")
        lines.append(f"dictionary encoding({enc}) byteorder({bo}) using {qstr(r, data_name)} {{")
    else:
        lines.append(f"dictionary using {qstr(r, data_name)} {{")
    return lines


def gen_var_numeric(r: random.Random, start_col: int, idx: int) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    tname, _ = r.choice(NUMERIC_TYPES)
    vname = rand_ident(r, f"n{idx}")
    fmt = r.choice(FMT_NUMERIC) if r.random() < 0.8 else None
    label = None
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        label = qstr(r, f"Numeric var {idx}")
    pieces = [f"  _column({start_col}) {tname} {vname}"]
    if fmt:
        pieces.append(qstr(r, fmt))
    if label:
        pieces.append(f"label({label})")
    line = ' '.join(pieces)
    # Advance column by a plausible display width to avoid overlap; use 10-14
    advance = r.randint(8, 14)
    return line, start_col + advance


def gen_var_string(r: random.Random, start_col: int, idx: int) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    vname = rand_ident(r, f"s{idx}")
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # strL variant without explicit width or format
        pieces = [f"  _column({start_col}) strL {vname}"]
        advance = r.randint(10, 20)
    else:
        width = r.choice(STRING_WIDTH_CHOICES)
        pieces = [f"  _column({start_col}) str{width} {vname}"]
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            fmt = r.choice(FMT_STRING)
            # Ensure width-compatible numeric part in format if applicable
            if fmt.endswith('s') and fmt != "%s":
                try:
                    n = int(fmt.strip('%s').strip('%'))
                except Exception:
                    n = width
                # clamp
                n = max(1, min(width, n))
                fmt = f"%{n}s"
            pieces.append(qstr(r, fmt))
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            pieces.append(f"label({qstr(r, f'String var {idx} label')})")
        advance = max(2, width)
    line = ' '.join(pieces)
    return line, start_col + advance


def gen_misc_lines(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    lines = []
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append("  // inline comment")
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append("  /* block comment */")
    return lines


def build_dictionary(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a dummy data filename; fuzzer will map it to a generated file path
    data_name = "data.txt"
    lines: List[str] = gen_header(r, data_name)

    start_col = r.randint(1, 5)
    var_count = r.randint(5, 16)

    # Mix numeric and string variables
    for i in range(var_count):
        lines.extend(gen_misc_lines(r))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            line, start_col = gen_var_numeric(r, start_col, i)
        else:
            line, start_col = gen_var_string(r, start_col, i)
        lines.append(line)
        # Occasionally skip columns to create gaps
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            start_col += r.randint(1, 5)

    # Optional terminator comments and closing brace
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append("  // end vars")
    lines.append("}")

    # Prepend a note as a comment occasionally
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lines.insert(0, "/* Stata dictionary generated for fuzzing */")

    text = "\n".join(l for l in lines if l is not None) + "\n"
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    dct = build_dictionary(r)
    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    b = dct.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

# This generator focuses on producing short ASCII/UTF-8 C strings that are
